newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican bombers hit French mainland targets.
newsitem.headline: Corsican bombers hit French mainland targets.

text.p: Corsican separatists claimed responsibility on Thursday for two overnight bombings in the southern French city of Nimes, a few hours after a leading nationalist was sentenced to prison for carrying guns.

A caller told a local television station that the outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC), making rare attacks on mainland France, planted bombs which caused damage but no casualties at a tax office and courthouse in Nimes.

Two others exploded in Corsica overnight, one at a courthouse in l'Ile Rousse, a town of which Veterans Affairs Minister Pierre Pasquini is mayor, and another at a discotheque in Ajaccio, the French Mediterranean island's capital.
Both did extensive damage but injured no one.
An appeals court in Bastia sentenced the leader of the most militant separatist group, Francois Santoni, in his absence on Wednesday to four months in jail, with another eight months suspended.
Santoni, secretary-general of A Cuncolta Naziunalista, the legal front for the FLNC's Historical Wing, is in hiding.
In an apparent act of retaliation, an unknown attacker threw an incendiary device into the entrance of the Bastia courthouse on Thursday, but caused no damage.

An FLNC "truce", declared in January but breached by dozens of bombings on the island, expired last Saturday, a week after the movement planted a bomb at Prime Minister Alain Juppe's mayoral office in the southwestern French city of Bordeaux.

Juppe responded by vowing to crack down on separatist gunmen and put "Corsican terrorism" out of action. Street patrols, random roadblocks and guards on public buildings have been increased but but so far there has been no roundup of known militants.
